change.headline: Tuscany and Florence swapped places
change.summary: The original order drove north past Florence to Val d'Orcia, doubled back up to Florence, then ran the full length of the country south to Naples. Reversing the middle two stops makes Florence the northernmost point and puts Val d'Orcia directly on the way south — roughly two hours less time in the car, and the Tuscan countryside now decompresses you between two dense cities instead of sitting between them.
wins: Florence becomes the turning point; every leg after it runs south.
Siena joins the trip — it sits squarely on the new Florence → Val d'Orcia drive and cost nothing to add.
Val d'Orcia now leads into Rome/Naples rather than backtracking to Florence, saving ~2 hrs of driving.
Three unhurried country days land in the middle of the trip instead of two city stops back to back.
costs: The Rome → Florence transfer keeps the Orvieto stop but arrives mid-afternoon, so the Accademia and the Duomo climb move to Fri Aug 28 alongside the Uffizi — Florence's one full day is now genuinely full.
Trattoria Mario (lunch only) no longer fits anywhere and is demoted to an alternate.
The Val d'Orcia and Brunello days had to trade places so the wineries don't land on a Sunday.

days.title: Landing in Rome
days.kicker: ROME — Hotel Trame, by the Pantheon
days.note: Jet-lag day. Nothing ticketed, nothing timed — the only fixed point is dinner.

items.title: Land at FCO
items.detail: Immigration + bags, about 45 min

items.title: Private transfer to the hotel
items.detail: Pre-booked car, roughly 45 min into the centro storico

items.title: Check in at Hotel Trame
items.detail: A former Franciscan monastery a few streets off Campo de' Fiori

items.title: First walk: Pantheon → Piazza Navona → Campo de' Fiori
items.detail: The Pantheon is an eight-minute walk. Go before the nap, not after.

items.title: Nap, deliberately
items.detail: Set an alarm. This is the single best defence against day-two jet lag.

items.title: Aperitivo at Etabli
items.detail: Or the Campari bar on Campo de' Fiori

items.title: Dinner — Armando al Pantheon
items.detail: Tiny, family-run, and booked out weeks ahead. Reserve now.

days.title: The Vatican, before anyone else
days.note: Early entry is the whole point: the Sistine Chapel is a different room with 40 people in it than with 400.

items.title: Vatican early-entry private tour
items.detail: Into the Sistine Chapel before general admission

items.title: Lunch — Da Romolo or Hostaria Dino e Tony
items.detail: Unfussy Roman cooking a short walk from the museum exit

items.title: Back to the hotel through the heat
items.detail: Late August in Rome peaks around 3pm. Don't fight it.

items.title: Castel Sant'Angelo, then the bridge at sunset
items.detail: Ponte Sant'Angelo with Bernini's angels catching the last light

items.title: Rooftop aperitivo near Campo de' Fiori
OPERA — arias at All Saints' Anglican Church
items.detail: Confirm the Aug 25 programme; Via del Babuino, off Piazza di Spagna

items.title: Late dinner — Pierluigi
items.detail: Seafood on Piazza de' Ricci; a properly Roman hour to eat

days.title: Ancient Rome, end to end
days.note: Last Roman day before the north. The Borghese slot is optional and needs its own timed ticket.

items.title: Colosseum with arena floor, then Forum + Palatine
items.detail: The arena-floor add-on is worth it — you stand where the sand was

items.title: Lunch — Roscioli
items.detail: Carbonara and cacio e pepe, and the deli counter on the way out
items.how: Walk, 5 min via Campo de' Fiori

items.title: Trastevere on foot
items.detail: Cross the Tiber and wander to Piazza Santa Maria in Trastevere

items.title: Optional — Galleria Borghese
items.detail: Timed entry, two-hour slots, books out early. Skip it guilt-free if the day already feels long.

items.title: Dinner — Da Enzo al 29
items.detail: Trastevere, twelve tables, no reservations after 9pm

days.title: North to Florence, by way of Orvieto
days.changeNote: Was Rome → Tuscany. The Orvieto lunch stop survives the swap; it sits on the A1 between Rome and Florence either way.
days.warn: Tight evening. The 8:00pm opera assumes the car reaches Florence by 4pm — hold the driver to a 2:00pm departure from Orvieto. If the drive slips, move the opera to Fri Aug 28 and pull Borgo San Jacopo forward to tonight.

items.title: Check out; driver-guide pickup
items.detail: North on the A1

items.title: Orvieto — the Duomo and lunch
items.detail: A hilltop Umbrian town with one of the great striped façades in Italy. Ninety minutes is enough.
items.how: Just off the A1, ~1h15 from Rome

items.title: Back on the road — hold this departure
items.detail: Orvieto → Florence is about two hours

items.title: Check in — Casa G. Firenze
items.detail: Via dei Rondinelli, between the Duomo and Santa Maria Novella

items.title: Unpack and reset
items.detail: You have been in a car since morning

items.title: Aperitivo on the secret patio
items.detail: Casa G.'s courtyard bar

items.title: OPERA — La Traviata at St. Mark's Anglican
items.detail: Via Maggio, across Ponte Santa Trinita. Moved here from Aug 30 by the reorder — rebook the date.

items.title: Dinner — Trattoria Sostanza
items.detail: Cash only. The butter chicken and the tortino. Alternative: Buca dell'Orafo.

days.title: All of Florence in one day
days.changeNote: Absorbs the Accademia and the Duomo climb from the old arrival day. Three timed entries before lunch — book all three now, in this order.
days.note: Dense by design. Everything before 1pm is ticketed and time-stamped; everything after is yours.

items.title: Accademia — David at first entry
items.detail: Forty-five minutes is genuinely enough. Go straight down the hall.

items.title: Duomo — climb Brunelleschi's dome
items.detail: 463 steps, timed slot, and much better before the day heats up

items.title: Coffee on Piazza della Signoria
items.detail: The Loggia dei Lanzi is an open-air sculpture hall and it is free

items.title: Uffizi, guided
items.detail: Botticelli, Leonardo, the Caravaggio room. Roughly two hours with a guide.

items.title: Lunch in the Oltrarno — Il Santo Bevitore
items.detail: Or Gucci Osteria if you want the splurge. Trattoria Mario is the third option if you'd rather eat near San Lorenzo.

items.title: Pitti Palace and the Boboli Gardens
items.detail: The gardens are the reason to go; climb to the top for the view back over the city

items.title: Oltrarno artisan workshops
items.detail: Via Maggio and Santo Spirito — gilders, leatherworkers, restorers still working street level

items.title: Ponte Vecchio, then up to Piazzale Michelangelo
items.detail: Sunset is around 8:00pm. Taxi up, walk down.

items.title: Dinner — Borgo San Jacopo
items.detail: Michelin-starred, on the river, with a handful of window tables. Ask for one.

days.title: Into the Val d'Orcia, through Siena
days.changeNote: Entirely new leg, and the clearest win of the reorder — Siena sits directly on the Florence → Val d'Orcia road and cost nothing to add.

items.title: Check out; driver south
items.detail: Florence → Siena is about 1h15 on the superstrada

items.title: Siena — Piazza del Campo
items.detail: The shell-shaped square where the Palio is run. Sit in it for ten minutes before doing anything else.

items.title: Siena Duomo and the Piccolomini Library
items.detail: The library frescoes are the surprise — most people walk past the door

items.title: Lunch in Siena
items.detail: Osteria Le Logge, just off the Campo, if you want to book something

items.title: South through the Crete Senesi
items.detail: Clay hills, bare ridgelines, and the first cypresses. Tell the driver you want photo stops.

items.title: Check in — Castello di Velona
items.detail: A hilltop castle with thermal springs and its own Brunello vineyard, looking straight down the Val d'Orcia

items.title: The thermal pools
items.detail: Natural hot springs on the terrace. This is what the castle is for.

items.title: Estate Brunello at sunset
items.detail: Aperitivo on the terrace as the valley goes gold

items.title: Dinner — Settimo Senso
items.detail: The castle's rooftop restaurant

days.title: The postcard drive
days.changeNote: Swapped with the Brunello day. A straight shift would have put the wineries on a Sunday, when most Montalcino estates are closed or appointment-only; the hill towns don't care what day it is.

items.title: Pienza
items.detail: A Renaissance pope's built-from-scratch ideal city, and the best pecorino in Italy. Walk the panoramic wall.

items.title: The cypress roads
items.detail: The winding drive below San Quirico — the shot everyone comes here for

items.title: Lunch — Latte di Luna in Pienza
items.detail: Or La Porta in Monticchiello, with a terrace over the valley

items.title: Montepulciano — Vino Nobile cellars
items.detail: Contucci under the Palazzo Comunale, or Avignonesi outside town

items.title: Bagno Vignoni
items.detail: A medieval village built around a steaming thermal pool where the piazza should be

items.title: Dinner — Osteria La Botte Piena
items.detail: Montefollonico. Open Sunday, closed Mondays — which is exactly why this day moved.

days.title: Brunello, all day
days.changeNote: Moved off Sunday so the estates are actually open. Confirm both winery appointments by phone or email — neither takes walk-ins.

items.title: Driver to Montalcino
items.detail: About thirty minutes up the hill

items.title: Winery one — Castello Banfi or Poggio Antico
items.detail: The big, polished estate visit: cellars, tour, structured tasting

items.title: Winery lunch, paired
items.detail: Long lunch with the Brunello poured alongside

items.title: Winery two — Casanova di Neri or Il Marroneto
items.detail: Deliberately small after the grand one. Il Marroneto makes maybe 15,000 bottles a year.

items.title: Enoteca La Fortezza
items.detail: Inside the Montalcino fortress walls — taste across producers you didn't visit

items.title: Something casual near the castle
items.detail: After a day of tasting, keep dinner short

days.title: The long haul south
days.kicker: TUSCANY → AMALFI, via Rome and Pompeii
days.changeNote: Replaces the old Florence → Naples train. Val d'Orcia is two hours from Rome, so you now pick up the Frecciarossa at Termini instead of doubling back to Florence.
days.warn: The longest day of the trip and the one with the least slack. Book the Frecciarossa seats and the Pompeii guide together, and give the driver the train time in writing.

items.title: Check out; driver toward Rome
items.detail: About 2h15 down to Termini

items.title: Roma Termini
items.detail: Buffer built in — aim to be on the platform 30 min early

items.title: Frecciarossa — Rome → Naples
items.detail: 1h10 to Napoli Centrale. Book seats, not just the fare.

items.title: Naples — driver meets the train
items.detail: Chinese driver-guide pickup at Napoli Centrale

items.title: Pompeii, guided
items.detail: Two hours is the right length in September heat. Ask for the Villa of the Mysteries.

items.title: Snack, then onto the corniche
items.detail: The coast road starts properly after Vietri

items.title: Check in — Anantara Convento di Amalfi
items.detail: A 13th-century monastery on the cliff edge, with the original cloister still standing

items.title: Dinner — Dei Cappuccini
items.detail: The hotel's Michelin room, or La Locanda for pizza if the day has beaten you

days.title: Capri, by private boat
days.note: Weather-dependent. The Blue Grotto only opens in a flat sea — treat it as a bonus, not a plan.

items.title: Private boat from the hotel jetty
items.detail: Lucibello, roughly seven hours with skipper

items.title: The Faraglioni, the grottoes, the swim coves
items.detail: Blue Grotto if the sea is calm enough to enter

items.title: Lunch — Da Paolino
items.detail: Under the lemon trees. Il Riccio is the Michelin alternative, on the cliff by the grotto.

items.title: The Piazzetta and the Gardens of Augustus
items.detail: Gelato on the terrace above Via Krupp

items.title: Cruise home, prosecco at sunset
items.detail: About forty minutes back along the coast

items.title: Dinner — La Conca del Sogno
items.detail: Reachable by boat, in a cove near Nerano. Or stay in on the cloister terrace.

days.title: Ravello, above everything
days.note: The Ravello Festival runs to Sep 5. Check tonight's programme — the stage is built out over the cliff at Villa Rufolo.

items.title: The beach club, by cliff lift
items.detail: A slow morning at sea level before the day starts properly

items.title: Lunch — Lo Scoglio
items.detail: Nerano. The original spaghetti alla Nerano, and worth the boat ride on its own.

items.title: Up to Ravello
items.detail: Forty-five minutes of switchbacks above the coast

items.title: Villa Cimbrone
items.detail: The Terrace of Infinity — a marble balustrade lined with busts, and a thousand-foot drop to the sea

items.title: RAVELLO FESTIVAL — check the Sep 3 programme
items.detail: Confirmed concerts run to Sep 5. The Aug 29 Mahler Youth Orchestra date falls on your Florence → Siena transfer, so it is out either way.

items.title: Late dinner — Il Flauto di Pan
items.detail: In the Villa Cimbrone gardens. Rossellinis is the other option.

items.title: Check out; last look at the coast
Driver to Naples
items.detail: Coast road, then the A3

items.title: Check in — De Bonart, Curio Collection
items.detail: An art palazzo on Via Partenope in Chiaia, facing the bay

items.title: Naples Archaeological Museum
items.detail: Where everything good from Pompeii actually ended up. Go after seeing the site, not before.

items.title: Spaccanapoli
items.detail: The dead-straight Greek road that still splits the old city in half

items.title: Street food, standing up
items.detail: Pizza fritta, zeppoline, a sfogliatella riccia straight from the oven

items.title: Rooftop aperitivo
items.detail: Vesuvius on one side, the bay on the other

items.title: Dinner — Palazzo Petrucci
items.detail: Michelin-starred Neapolitan tasting menu

items.title: Pizza for breakfast
items.detail: Sorbillo or Di Matteo on Via dei Tribunali. Yes, at 9am. It's Naples.

items.title: Frecciarossa — Naples → Rome
items.detail: 1h15 to Termini

items.title: Check in — The St. Regis Rome
items.detail: Five minutes from Termini. Marriott Bonvoy.

items.title: Last Roman afternoon
items.detail: Piazza di Spagna and the windows along Via Condotti

items.title: Aperitivo at Lumen
items.detail: The St. Regis bar — the grand-hotel version of a last night

items.title: Farewell dinner — Aroma
items.detail: A rooftop table level with the top tier of the Colosseum. Imago is the alternative, over the Spanish Steps.

items.title: Private transfer to FCO
items.detail: About forty minutes on an empty Sunday road

items.title: Check in and bag drop
items.detail: Three hours ahead for an intercontinental departure

items.title: FCO → IAH
items.detail: Arrivederci, Italia.

bookings.item: Montalcino winery appointments for Mon Aug 31

Piazzale Michelangelo at sunset; Ponte Vecchio at dawn; the Uffizi loggia
Cypress roads at golden hour; the Pienza walls; the castle vineyard
Positano's pastel stairs and Spiaggia Grande; Amalfi Drive viewpoints; the Ravello gardens

photographersNote: Trip.com has no reliable Italy 旅拍 listings. flags.title: Rome finale hotel had two different names
flags.detail: The Hotels tab said “The Edition”, while the itinerary, the drivers tab and the booking link all said The St. Regis Rome. Normalised to St. Regis — still Marriott Bonvoy, so the loyalty note holds.

flags.title: Lodging total disagreed with itself
flags.detail: The Budget tab carried 12,270 against the Hotels tab's 12,720. The hotel rows add to 12,720; the budget line was the typo.

flags.title: Photographers tab day numbers were stale
flags.detail: It listed Amalfi as days 4–6 and Florence as 11–12, which matched no version of the route. Renumbered against the new order.

flags.title: Overview route line omitted Tuscany entirely
flags.detail: The old Route row jumped Rome → Florence → Amalfi with no Val d'Orcia in it.

flags.title: Stale hotel names on the bookings tab
flags.detail: It referenced a “Nomos Hotel Rome” (your Rome hotel is Hotel Trame) and a doubled “De Bonart Naples Naples”. Cleaned up in the rebuild.

flags.title: Aug 27 is the tightest evening of the trip
flags.detail: A 4.5-hour drive with a stop, then an 8pm curtain. Hold the driver to a 2pm departure from Orvieto, or swap the opera to Aug 28.

flags.title: Sep 1 has almost no slack
flags.detail: Driver, train, guided Pompeii and the corniche in one day. A missed Frecciarossa cascades into a night arrival at the Convento.
